Read more Tom Gralish / Staff Photographer by Robert Moran Updated  Nov. 16, 2026, 6:28 p.m. ET | Published  Nov. 16, 2026, 6:24 p.m. ET Listen to article •   0:00 min The remains of a 37-year-old woman reported missing two years ago have been recovered in Burlington County , and the investigation into her death is continuing, the New Jersey State Police said Monday.
 Danielle Lopez disappeared while she was camping with her boyfriend in New Jersey’s Brendan T. Byrne State Forest. Lopez was recorded on surveillance video on the morning of April 13, 2024, buying coffee at a Wawa not far from the campground.
 NBC’s Dateline show reported on her case .
 Investigators said witnesses reported last seeing Lopez that evening walking alone on Lost Lane deep in the Pine Barrens.
 Lopez’s mother reported her missing 11 days later on April 24.
 On Saturday, the New Jersey State Police Major Crime South Unit and the Missing Persons Unit coordinated a multiagency search operation within the Brendan T. Byrne State Forest in Chatsworth, Burlington County, as part of the investigation of Lopez’s disappearance.
 “During the search operation, human remains were discovered. Following a thorough forensic examination, the remains were positively identified today as those of Danielle Lopez,” the state police said . 
 No other details about the investigation were released.
 Anyone with information about Lopez’s disappearance can contact the New Jersey State Police Missing Persons Unit at 609-882-2000 ext. 2554.
 Lopez’s boyfriend, James Scott Dunn, spoke to police shortly after she was reported missing and he was arrested in an unrelated drug case. In late 2025, Dunn was sentenced to five years in prison.
 In a prison interview with The Inquirer last year , Dunn said he and Lopez were “homeless” and living in hotels before moving to the campground. Dunn said he was away from the campground when Lopez disappeared, and when he returned the campground was in “disarray.”
